Install 1bit OS#

1bit OS is the Puppy Linux appliance in os/README.md: Lemonade Server with this engine inside, our MOK-signed kernel, headless by default. It runs from the stick it was written to, and it can install itself onto a disk: 1bit-install copies the system you booted, so an install downloads nothing.

what you want how what it erases
try it, keep nothing boot the stick — run from the stick nothing on the machine
run it from the internal disk sudo 1bit-install <disk> --yes on the stick that disk, all of it
carry it on another USB drive the same command onto that drive that drive, all of it
keep the OS already on the machine not in this release — see 4 —
add the engine to an existing Linux the engine package — see 5 nothing

What you need#
stick 16 GB or more: the image is 9,128,902,656 bytes (8.5 GiB) and the data partition takes the rest of the stick
image 1bit-os-puppy.img.xz + SHA256SUMS from Hugging Face; the releases page carries the lemonade-onebit package and the release notes
machine an AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo) box, the machine this release is built and tested on
firmware UEFI, Secure Boot on (see 6)

The image is on Hugging Face, not on the GitHub release, because a GitHub release asset is capped at 2 GiB and this one is 9,128,902,656 B written (2,212,389,580 B as .img.xz). Fetch both files, check the checksum, then write it and prepare it (the last line is what puts the API key, your SSH key and any models on the stick — see 1):

# 1bit-os-puppy.img.xz and SHA256SUMS from https://huggingface.co/1bit-MONSTER/1bit-OS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
xz -dc 1bit-os-puppy.img.xz | sudo dd of=/dev/sdX bs=4M conv=fsync status=progress
sudo os/mini/prepare-stick.sh /dev/sdX --mint --ssh-pubkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

Writing the .img.xz straight from balenaEtcher or Rufus (DD mode) is the same write with no shell line, but the prepare-stick line below is still what puts the API key on the stick.

prepare-stick writes /ssh/authorized_keys and a freshly minted Lemonade API key into /lemonade/lemond.conf on the stick's 1BIT-DATA partition, and copies --model files into /models. A stick written with dd alone has no API key: the appliance boots, but Lemonade says so in its log and serves every endpoint unauthenticated (Serving on non-loopback host '0.0.0.0' without an API key ... all endpoints ... are reachable from other machines unauthenticated), which is why --mint is part of the protocol. That the appliance does not mint one itself when the file is empty is a defect of this image (#867); until it is fixed, treat --mint as mandatory, and check a stick you did not prepare with sudo sed -n 's/^LEMONADE_API_KEY=//p' /data/lemonade/lemond.conf — an empty answer means open.

1. Run from the stick (no install)#

  1. Put the stick in the machine. On the Bosgame BeyondMax use the front USB-A port (7).
  2. Boot it. The default entry, 1bit OS (headless console, 7.3.0-rc4-1bit-perfopt+), comes up headless: a console with no X. The second entry, 1bit OS (desktop, JWM), starts Puppy's desktop on the same system; the third, 1bit OS - serial root shell, gives a root shell on the serial port for a rack machine with no monitor.
  3. Nothing on the machine is written. The system runs in RAM from the stick's squashfs (pfix=copy); the models, Lemonade's config and cache, your SSH keys and the API key live on the stick's 1BIT-DATA partition.

Check that it is up:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(sudo sed -n 's/^LEMONADE_API_KEY=//p' /data/lemonade/lemond.conf)" \
     http://127.0.0.1:13305/api/v1/models

That command is one of the ones measured below; a client on another machine uses the box's address instead of 127.0.0.1 (Connect a client).

What persists on the stick, all of it on 1BIT-DATA (Puppy's save layer, PUPMODE=12): models/, lemonade/config/, lemonade/cache/, lemonade/lemond.conf (the API key), ssh/ (host key and authorized_keys), npu/kernels/, cache/hrx-jit/. A file written elsewhere (/etc, /root, /tmp) lives in RAM: measured, a marker written in /etc and then poweroff -f was gone on the next boot, while the same boot's marker on /data was still there.

2. Install to an internal disk#

From the running stick:

lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL,MOUNTPOINT      # find the disk: model and size, never the stick
sudo 1bit-install /dev/nvme0n1 --yes

/dev/nvme0n1 is an example: pass the disk you mean to erase. The installer refuses to continue unless the argument is a whole disk, it is not the disk this system booted from, and none of its partitions is mounted — and it prints the disk's model, its size and its current partition table, then waits 10 seconds before writing:

1bit OS install
  target : /dev/nvme0n1  (Samsung SSD 990 PRO 2TB, 2000.4 GB)
  booted from: /dev/sda (/dev/sda2) - refused as a target
  source : ESP /dev/sda1, frugal install + data /data
  anything on /dev/nvme0n1 is about to be destroyed:
    ...
  writing in 10 s (Ctrl-C now and nothing has been touched)

It erases the target disk. What it writes, in its own seven steps:

step what
1 a GPT with a 512 MiB EFI system partition (vfat, label 1BIT-OS) and a 1BIT-DATA ext4 partition filling the rest
2 the formats, mkfs.vfat and mkfs.ext4 with a fresh UUID for the data partition
3 the boot chain copied from the stick's own ESP: BOOTX64.EFI (shim), grubx64.efi, mmx64.efi (MokManager) and grub.cfg
4 the whole data partition — the frugal install /1bit (vmlinuz, initrd.gz, the four squashfs files) and /data (models, Lemonade's config and cache, the API key, SSH keys) — plus .installed and install.log
5 grub.cfg re-pointed at this disk: search --fs-uuid <uuid> and every entry pinned with pupsfs=UUID=<uuid> 1bit.data=UUID=<uuid>, because two 1BIT-DATA labels exist once a machine is installed
6 a read-back: the kernel's sha256 on the new disk must equal the source's, initrd.gz and the SFS files must be there
7 a firmware boot entry via efibootmgr, label 1bit OS, pointing at the new ESP, put first in BootOrder

Then power off, remove the stick, and boot. The firmware's boot menu lists 1bit OS; if the machine comes up in its own menu instead of booting, pick it there once.

On the cycle-13 image the installed disk does not boot yet. The install itself is complete and correct, but two defects stop the first boot: installer step 5 writes pupsfs=UUID=<uuid>, which Puppy's init does not resolve (#865), and step 7's BootNext lands on the firmware's own boot-manager entry instead of the new one (#866). Both are in the appliance lane for the release; until they land, boot the installed disk by editing its grub.cfg entry to pupsfs=1BIT-DATA 1bit.data=UUID=<uuid> — measured to boot, with the models and the API key in place.

Check the result from the installed system:

lsblk -f                                  # ESP 1BIT-OS + 1BIT-DATA on the target
sudo blkid /dev/nvme0n1*                  # the ESP is vfat, the data partition the UUID grub pinned
efibootmgr -v | grep "1bit OS"            # the firmware entry, pointing at this disk's ESP

The installer ends by telling you to run 1bit-release-check, which says INSTALLED and runs the same rows as the stick. The install log is on the installed 1BIT-DATA partition as /install.log.

3. Install to another USB drive#

The same command, pointed at the drive instead of an internal disk:

lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL,TRAN              # TRAN usb: which drive is which
sudo 1bit-install /dev/sdb --yes           # the stick is /dev/sda, so this is the other one

It is the same installer with the same refusals and the same seven steps; the target may be USB, SATA or NVMe, it only has to be a whole disk that is not the one you booted. Afterwards boot the machine from that drive (the firmware entry it wrote points at it): it is the same system, portable, with the models and the API key carried across.

The stick you installed from is untouched, so you can keep it as the installer/recovery stick.

4. Keep the system already on the machine#

There is no dual-boot wizard in this release, and there is no "install alongside" mode. The installer takes one whole disk and erases it. What that means per case:

the machine today what to do
one disk you want to keep install to a second disk (option 2), or to a USB drive (option 3) and boot that
a disk with nothing you need install over it (option 2)
a Windows machine you want to keep intact install to another disk or a USB drive; the appliance does not touch the Windows disk, and the firmware's own boot menu is how you go back

The installer does not shrink, move or resize any partition, and it writes nothing to a disk you did not name. It does add its own firmware entry, 1bit OS, which the firmware's boot menu then offers next to the other OS.

5. The engine on an existing Linux (advanced)#

The supported install for this release is the appliance: 1bit OS carries the kernel, the NPU driver, the signed modules and the HRX runtime that the engine needs, and a plain distribution does not. What exists for an existing Linux:
Lemonade with the engine as its backend the lemonade-onebit package from the releases page, for a machine already running Lemonade (Lemonade)
the engine alone, packaged for a distribution scripts/mk-plugin-package.sh builds 1bit-engine_<version>_amd64.deb and a tarball and wires a stock Lemonade to it (PR #860)

Both are advanced, and not the supported path for this release: they put the engine on a system whose kernel, amdxdna driver and HSA runtime we did not choose, so the device rows of 1bit-release-check are yours to run. There is no PPA route in this release — it is parked.

6. Secure Boot and our MOK#

The stick and the install boot with Secure Boot on: shim → our MOK-signed grub → our MOK-signed kernel (7.3.0-rc4-1bit-perfopt+) → our signed modules (amdgpu, amdxdna, ec_su_axb35). Verified on the shipped image: sbverify --cert MOK-Kernel.pem /1bit/vmlinuz → Signature verification OK.

your machine what to do
our key is already enrolled (the box this release is tested on) nothing — boot it
our key is not enrolled the firmware will refuse the kernel. Turn Secure Boot off in the firmware setup for now: the system runs, everything works, and Secure Boot is a signature check, not a feature of the appliance
you want Secure Boot on anyway enroll the public key with mokutil --import MOK-Kernel.der from an OS already installed on that machine, reboot, and confirm in MokManager (Enroll MOK → Continue → Yes → password)

The release does not put the certificate on the stick — measured: the ESP carries BOOTX64.EFI, grubx64.efi, mmx64.efi and grub.cfg, and the image carries no .der file — so a machine without our key cannot enroll it from the stick alone. The signing key and what is signed with it are in Linux kernel.

Check the state on a booted system:

mokutil --sb-state          # SecureBoot enabled
mokutil --list-enrolled | grep -i "1bit\|strixhalo"

7. The Bosgame BeyondMax has one usable USB port#

On the Bosgame BeyondMax (AXB35-02, BIOS 1.09) only the front USB-A port works under Linux: a drive plugged into the front or rear Type-C, or a rear USB-A port, produces no kernel event at all — the xHCI port registers stay in RxDetect, and three of the four controllers have taken no interrupt. The same ports work in Windows on the same box, so it is a firmware/EC gap, not a driver in this image (#823). Boot from the front USB-A port.

What was verified for this page#

On the cycle-13 image (sha256 dcc619ff74882f484e4c7dfb373980f294ce2f39b02291fb816ac7c62776beb7, 9,128,902,656 B) in QEMU with Secure Boot on and our MOK in db, kernel 7.3.0-rc4-1bit-perfopt+:

claim measured
the image boots to Lemonade with Secure Boot on boot, lemond on 0.0.0.0:13305, web app on /, ssh on 22, kernel signature OK
1bit-install refuses the disk it booted from 1bit-install: REFUSED: /dev/sda is the disk this system booted from (/dev/sda2 is on it), exit 2, the stick's UUIDs unchanged afterwards
an install to a bare disk completes all seven steps, exit 0: GPT 1BIT-OS 512 MiB + 1BIT-DATA 7.5 GiB, grub.cfg pinned to the new UUID, kernel sha256 read back equal, .installed and install.log written
the firmware entry is written efibootmgr lists 1bit OS → HD(1,GPT,<new ESP>)/\EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI (id 0004, not the 0000 the step's own log line printed — #866)
what the install copies the installed data partition holds /1bit (vmlinuz, initrd.gz, the four SFS), /data with the models, lemonade/ and ssh/, and .installed
boot of the installed disk as written fails on this image: init says Partition UUID=<uuid> not found and drops to the rescue console (#865)
boot of the same disk with pupsfs=1BIT-DATA (label) instead of pupsfs=UUID=… boots: puppypc20143, /data/.installed present, lemond up, GET /api/v1/models 401 without the key and 200 with it
the boot device is rejected, not guessed the refusal above is by device: /proc/mounts names /dev/sda2 as /data, and the installer resolves the disk behind it
pmedia=usbhd is not the cause the failed boot was from a USB device, where pmedia=usbhd is the correct media class; the label/UUID A/B above isolates the cause to the UUID form

Not verified here: an install to a real internal NVMe on the hardware (the install gate in Releases covers it), the firmware's own boot menu on a non-QEMU machine, and Secure Boot enrolment on a machine without our key (the table above is the documented route, not a measurement of it). The image used was the cycle-13 artifact, not the next release's.
